4. The matter of funding to implement the program is discussed in general terms. Participation of the states is also generally outlined. The magnitude of this program and the budgetary implications are such that specifics on both - funding and state participation - should be included in your statement.
Comments which follow reflect our reaction to specific portions of your draft.
There is an inherent semantic problem associated with the word "extinct". To many, this word carries the implication that the species is no longer in existence. A species (or subspecies) threatened with extinction, therefore, is one in danger of disappearing from the face of the earth. The word "extirpate" has a connotation, which more accurately describes the situation experienced by many endangered species, especially as it relates to their disappearance or dimunition on a portion of their traditional range. We request that you consider substituting the word "extirpation" for "extinction" throughout your text, where applicable, to more clearly define the status of many species. A short glossary might be included in a preface to define these and other terms for the reader.
We find a similar problem with references to "subspecies". A clear definition of this word and the context within which it is used is essential. Many subspecies can be identified only by taxonomic characteristics which almost require sacrifice of the animal to find these characteristics. In addition, sometimes the integradations which occur over a geographic area are almost impossible to describe. Perhaps "race", "form" or another word, along with specific location data on the range of the animal might be used to help clarify what could be an extremely confusing situation.
A more definitive explanation of "likely within the forseeable future to become threatened with extinction" is needed. This phrase is extremely speculative and vague; judgements made on this criterion would lack credibility. Also this phrase when tied to the words "subspecies" and "extinction" (as we have already discussed them) lacks the preciseness required in a scientific approach to this important problem.
In our opinion the first sentence of your section "Description of the Environment" tends to overstate the scope of the problem. We feel this sentence: "Endangered species occupy / the total spectrum of / the Earth's habitats from the arctic regions to the equator, including / all the / ecotypes from alpine to marine." would be more accurate if the bracketed words were deleted.
Your opening paragraph in the section "Environmental Impact of the Proposed Action" portrays the role and significance of individual species in their ecosystems. We do not argue with this. We do recommend, however, that resolving of problems encountered by endangered species must not be based solely upon protection of that species. The importance of the need for study and fostering of all components of ecosystems within which the endangered animal exists the importance of the need for study animal exists.
